title: How are you guys getting such detailed games out of Astra?
author: No_Departure7494
selftext:
I wasn't expecting much but after seeing the results on this sub, I decided to give it a shot.

"Give me a ridiculously detailed city with this, that, etc".

The images on here show detailed cars, lighting, etc.

For me it just pumped out a grid with tons of generic shapes meant to be buildings or something haha. Looks like absolute shit.

comments.author: KnownPride
comments.body: By not one shoting it and go into detail and  put in real work.

replies.author: No_Departure7494
replies.body: Yeah but that involves effort and I want to one shot it with AI as advertised on twitter.

replies.author: No-Masterpiece4010
replies.body: That is crazy, who advertised this to you on twitter

comments.author: geddy
comments.body:
I've put together a few smaller games and I've found that while this is amazing technology, it's all so open ended what you can come out with on the other side that it requires loads of iteration, especially for the tiniest details. A human would add those tiny details, the robot does not, until you ask it specifically.

If anything it made me appreciate just how specific the "little things" are that actually make a game look good.

comments.body: Start with meshy to generate pictures ,then generate 3d model , then have astra refine it by decimating baking, water tightening , fixing it up etc .

comments.author: Wheelydope
comments.body: Invest in asset packs for the game style you’re making. I’d also highly recommend buying a large audio collection for sound effects. It will dramatically change your output if you’re using finalized art assets. Then you do a ton of mechanic tweaking, animations, etc through tons of prompts and play testing feedback to the model.

comments.author: Snoo-29395
comments.body:
By not telling "Give me a ridiculously detailed city with this, that, etc"

\- Look at this buildings  
\- See the very basic darwing i made  
\- Create a concept art of the drawing + the inspirations  
\- Adjust the concept  
\- Now make it on blender  
\- Adjust it until is right  
\- Move to the next building

You are supose to be a "director". You can't tell your team "build me a big city" and expect it to be right, you need context, iteration, make the team understand your idea, same thing applies to AI

comments.author: baathus
comments.body: By doing the exact oposit to this. I develop the game in my head for days, then I describe it very detailed, multiple pages of text. Then I ask AI to analyse the plan, point out flaws, then we iterate. It's a long process, and it takes hours and days. The sooner people start realizing this and stops expecting AI to magically invent a full game from nothing, the sooner we will start seeing a decline in slop-games.

comments.author: GratefulForGarcia
comments.body:
1) Generate image  
2) Upload image to Meshy for 3D model  
3) Connect Claude/GPT to Blender MCP so it can optimize/rig/animate model

I don’t go below High effort on either LLM and if an animation isn’t going so well I’ll crank the effort up
